basis: Inherited motor neuron degeneration; weakness and respiratory failure reflect denervation rather than primary muscle or lung disease.
Optic disc malformation, macular atrophy and chorioretinal disease directly impair vision.
Pituitary GH excess defines pathological skeletal overgrowth; cardiac hypertrophy/cardiomyopathy is reported at 80-99% in supplied HPO.
Disease of the lips, which are part of the mouth; no common mechanism applies across this umbrella.
Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; neurologic dysfunction, hepatopathy and sensorineural hearing loss each commonly exceed 30%; retinal disease omitted under cap.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy with defining episodic hyperkalemia; no primary CNS injury. Cardiac and respiratory complications are occasional.
Oral and digital malformations plus neurodevelopmental disease define OFD1; cystic kidney dysplasia in 3/7 (~43%). Common skin findings omitted under cap.
Retrocerebellar arachnoid cyst is a structural malformation of the central nervous system.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and language delay in 3/3; short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by growth, bone maturation and joint abnormalities; developmental stagnation alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Neoplasm arises in vulvar reproductive epithelium; no reproductive organ axis is available.
Malignancy of the ocular choroid; vascular ancestry does not establish a separate cardiovascular disease.
UBQLN2-associated motor neuron degeneration, sometimes with frontotemporal dementia; both affect the neurologic axis.
CAD-related pyrimidine metabolic defect causes encephalopathy; anemia in 5/5 and abnormal red-cell morphology in 6/6. RTA in one patient lacks prevalence evidence.
Congenital accessory mitral valve structures are a cardiac malformation; embolic injury is an occasional complication.
Neurodevelopmental impairment is nearly universal; skeletal anomalies are explicitly defining despite individual malformations occurring in only 3/19.
Intellectual disability and fibrosing/cholestatic hepatopathy define GRIDHH; sensorineural hearing loss in 1/3 (~33%), with limited sample certainty.
Idiopathic steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome is immune-mediated glomerular disease with focal segmental sclerosis.
Inherited complement deficiency; meningococcal disease is a separate infection to which patients are predisposed.
Benign neoplasm of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the available axes.
CACNA1A-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; nystagmus reflects neurologic dysfunction without established ocular damage.
Platelet storage-pool bleeding disorder with ocular/oculocutaneous albinism; pulmonary fibrosis excluded by definition and colitis is not common across these subtypes.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disease causing optic neuropathy; extraocular neurologic, muscle and cardiac manifestations are generally under 30%.
Isolated inherited dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced ventricular function and heart failure.
Umbrella of progressive skeletal muscle dystrophies; cardiac and other organ involvement varies by subtype and is not established across most patients.
